questions.question: State three rules for resistors connected in parallel.
questions.expected_answer: The voltage across each branch equals the source voltage; the current divides at junctions and the branch currents add up to the total current; adding resistors in parallel decreases the total resistance, so the total current increases.

questions.question: The current from a battery is 0,5 A. One branch of a parallel circuit carries 0,2 A. Find the current in the other branch and explain your reasoning.
questions.expected_answer: 0,5 − 0,2 = 0,3 A. The current divides at the junction and the branch currents add up to the total current, because charge is not created or lost at a junction.

questions.question: Give two advantages of wiring house lights in parallel rather than in series.
questions.expected_answer: Each light gets the full mains voltage, so it is fully bright; each can be switched on and off independently; if one bulb fails, the others stay on.
